statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits at 12 of 100 in the low band, thirteen points below the 25 block threshold, while stress remains extreme at 85 and confidence is high at 88.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The named danger window covers the August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC Michigan preliminary release, where the conditional path peaks at WATCH without reaching the block threshold.
headline: Three and a half hours of post-reopen trade leave NQ at 29,146.00, up 0.04%, with the 29,062.50 low held and bought back; tail eases to 12 while a 4.944% ten-year, VIX 17.84 and crude off its highs keep stress extreme at 85 into the August consumer price report.
body:
The overnight price path remains the cleanest evidence available and it continues to argue against a pathological regime. CME equity futures have been open for roughly three and a half hours since the 21:00 to 22:00 UTC maintenance halt. NQ trades 29,146.00, up 10.75 points or 0.04% against the 29,135.25 reference, inside a band of 29,062.50 to 29,171.50. That is 109 points, about 0.37%. The decisive detail is that the 29,062.50 low set in the previous hour was not revisited or extended: it held, price recovered through the middle of the band and now sits in the upper half with the day's change marginally positive. A low that holds and a probe that is retraced are the observable signature of working mean reversion, which is the opposite of the no-retracement path that tail risk measures. Tail therefore eases one point to 12 and the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON.

The backdrop remains genuinely difficult, which is why stress stays extreme at 85. The ten-year Treasury yield closed at 4.944%, up 10.7 basis points and its highest since 2023, against a two-year near 4.43% on the latest H.15 observation, a bear-steepening that tightens financial conditions directly on long-duration technology valuations. VIX closed at 17.84, up 8.38%, elevated in change terms though moderate in absolute level. U.S. equities fell for a fourth consecutive session on 10 September, with the S&P 500 down 0.58%, the Nasdaq Composite down 0.65% and the Dow down 0.6%. Producer prices rose 5.4% year-over-year, broadly in line. Futures pricing has carried meaningful odds of a Federal Reserve rate increase at the 15-16 September meeting, an unusual configuration that raises the sensitivity of every inflation print between now and then.

Energy is the one input improving at the margin. WTI trades 102.42 after a session high of 104.46, and Brent 107.57 after 110.19, so both benchmarks sit roughly two percent below their highs. The supply story behind them is unresolved: U.S. strikes on IRGC-linked tankers, Iranian missile fire at U.S. warships, Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities and Saudi output at its lowest since 1990. That is a structural stress condition rather than a current tail amplifier, and crude easing overnight removes one live source of directional pressure from the index.

The August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC is the session's dominant checkpoint, with consensus near 3.4% headline and 2.4% core year-over-year, followed by preliminary Michigan sentiment and inflation expectations at 14:00 UTC. Ahead of a release, hypothetical post-event alignment is not treated as observed structure. The conditional path therefore peaks at tail 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot, inside the watch band and below the block threshold, easing to 21 across the cash open and 20 through the Michigan release before decaying back into the low band as price discovery is assumed to become orderly. The named invalidation is explicit: shallow pullbacks with repeated extension after failed retracements would break that decay assumption. From 21:00 UTC the CME weekend closure removes the tradable path entirely and the conditional scores fall to a residual weekend-gap floor.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 01:00 UTC on 10 September to 00:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 10 and holds a tight 9 to 11 band through the U.S. overnight, the Asian session and the European morning, with the dominant mode recorded as mixed throughout. The regime change sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the August producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and the window peak of 24 at 13:00 UTC across the cash open, the only slot to reach the top of the watch band. It never crossed into the block threshold. From 14:00 UTC the series decays back into the low band at 17 and holds a 14 to 19 range through the U.S. afternoon and the close, with event/whipsaw recorded again at 20:00 and 21:00 UTC around the cash close and the maintenance halt. The final two hours settle at 15 and 14 as post-reopen trade proved contained. Stress never left the extreme band, rising from 80 to a peak of 87 and holding 86 through the last four hours, which is the clearest signal in the series: a difficult, high-volatility environment persisted for a full 24 hours without the price path ever becoming pathological.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens with roughly three and a half hours of observed post-reopen trade on 11 September and ends inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC the same day. Conditional tail starts at 12, holds 12 through the late Asian hours and settles at an 11 floor across the thinnest pre-European hours, where no U.S. macro is scheduled. From the European cash open it rebuilds gradually, 12 through 13, reaching 15 in the final full hour before the release as quoted depth thins. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot containing the August consumer price report, which stays inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold because an inflation surprise more reliably produces two-sided whipsaw than a sustained no-retracement path. It eases to 21 across the 13:30 UTC cash open and holds 20 through the 14:00 UTC Michigan preliminary release, the credible second information wave, then decays to 18 and back into the low band on the assumption that retracements reappear. The U.S. afternoon runs 16 down to 13 into the cash close. From 21:00 UTC the venue is shut and conditional tail drops to 9 and then a 7 weekend floor that represents gap risk at the Sunday reopen rather than any tradable intraday path. Stress stays extreme from 85 to a 92 peak at the release before stepping out of the extreme band only when the market closes. The decay after the release is an assumption, not an observation, and its named invalidation is shallow pullbacks with repeated extension after failed retracements.
